newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Only 5 Swiss francs in suspected old Nazi account.
newsitem.headline: Only 5 Swiss francs in suspected old Nazi account.

text.p: Switzerland's fourth-largest bank said on Monday an old account that might have been opened by a prominent Nazi contained only five Swiss francs ($3.30).
Zurich Kantonalbank (ZKB) also said it had given away to charity the contents of accounts that remained dormant for 20 years, totalling 580,000 Swiss francs over the years.

ZKB, which serves the city and canton of Zurich, said it had not finished a detailed examination of two accounts with potential Nazi links made public in a huge list of dormant pre-1945 accounts published by Swiss banks last week.
"There are five francs in an account under the name of Willi Bauer," Fritz Treichler, chief of staff to ZKB president Paul Hasenfratz, told Reuters.

Two of Switzerland's three biggest banks -- Union Bank of Switzerland UBS and Credit Suisse Group -- declined to comment on whether any suspected Nazi names were among the reported dormant accounts from their vaults.
But Swiss Bank Corp SBC said there were no known Nazi names on its account roster.
"We checked our dormant accounts against our own list of Nazi names. We found none of these names or the names from the Simon Wiesenthal Center," spokesman Michael Willi said.

ZKB's revelations came after Los Angeles-based Wiesenthal Center identified at least six names matching those of once-prominent Nazis on the list of nearly 1,800 Swiss accounts opened by foreigners before the end of World war Two in 1945.
Treichler said ZKB had two of these names on its rolls, Willi Bauer and Elise Eder. He could not say when they had opened accounts except that it was before May 1945.
Nazi-hunters said Bauer was an alias used by Anton Burger, an Eichmann aide and deputy commandant of the Theresienstadt concentration camp.
Elisabeth Eder was the wife of Ernst Kaltenbrunner, the head of the SD, the Nazis' intelligence arm.
Treichler said the Eder account, in the name of Elise rather than Elisabeth, might be a case of mistaken identity, he added.
"The reports said Elise Eder was the wife of Nazi official Ernst Kaltenbrunner and there is nothing in our records to reflect this," he said.
The other four possible Nazi names supplied by the Wiesenthal Center were Hermann Esser, Hermann Schmitz, Heinrich Hoffman and Karl Jager.

Swiss banks, under international pressure to find heirs for money left by victims of the Holocaust, made an unprecedented break with secrecy last Wednesday by publishing the list of dormant pre-1945 accounts.

While most banks insist they still have any assets that might have been forgotten since 1945, Zurich Kantonalbank said it had a policy of closing small accounts after 20 years of no contact with the customer.
The money was then given to charities, ZKB head Hasenfratz told the Zurich newspaper Tages-Anzeiger.
Hasenfratz said the bank would pay any claims that might still arise to the dissolved accounts. Bank reserves would cover the cost, he said.
"These were almost all smallish savings accounts," Treichler added.
ZKB is owned by the canton (state) of Zurich and had assets of 58.5 billion Swiss francs at the end of March. ($ = 1.518 Swiss Francs)
